title: Code World Model: Coding Agent as World Brain
hook: Video world models learn what happens, not why. Put a coding agent in charge of the rules — writing executable code that holds world state — and let the video model handle only the pixels.
key_points: Video-based world models learn dynamics from observations, which show outcomes rather than the rules producing them.
Code World Model separates world evolution from visual realization.
A coding agent acts as 'world brain': it reasons about events and emits executable code holding persistent state.
A proxy representation encodes frame-wise spatiotemporal constraints and compiles into a proxy video.
That proxy video conditions a video model to render the high-fidelity observation.
After fine-tuning on paired gameplay data, MiniMax-H3 follows the proxy specs while keeping visual detail.
content_html: World models aim to simulate how environments evolve under actions and events. The dominant approach learns that evolution from video — but video shows you outcomes, not the knowledge, rules, and mechanisms behind them. Chen, Lin, and Zhang argue that's why such models struggle to maintain persistent consequences or support coherent open-ended evolution: they never represented the rules in the first place.
extra_html:
Division of labour

Code World Model separates world evolution from visual realization. A coding agent serves as the world brain: it reasons about events and their consequences and generates executable code that maintains persistent world state and performs rule-consistent evolution. Code is a good substrate for this — state persists, rules are explicit and inspectable, and consequences compound the way they do in a real simulator. The video model is demoted to a renderer.

The interface

Connecting executable state to pixels is the hard part. The authors introduce a proxy representation that encodes frame-wise spatiotemporal constraints and compiles into a proxy video, which then conditions a video model to render high-fidelity observations. They also build data pipelines for constructing aligned proxy-observation pairs from gameplay and real-world video. After fine-tuning on paired gameplay data, MiniMax-H3 follows proxy-based spatiotemporal specifications from simple interactive worlds built by the coding agent while preserving rich visual detail and dynamics. The demonstrated worlds are simple, and that's the honest scope — but the split it argues for (code for persistence, video for realization) is a clean idea worth borrowing. arXiv, 2026.

related.title: World Models Meet Language Models
related.hook: A world model can imagine what happens next; an LLM can reason about it. The hard part is knowing when to trust the daydream — and when the simulation is just plausible nonsense.

related.title: Persistent Recursive Worlds Enable Autonomous Software Evolution
related.hook: Instead of keeping the agent alive across a long project, keep the project alive and let agents be disposable — enough to grow a 250k-line Rust C compiler for $44.

related.title: EchoWM: A World Model You Can Walk Into and Hear
related.hook: Most world models generate silent video. EchoWM generates 720p video plus environmental sound, music, and speech, and lets you navigate it continuously.

flashcards.prompt: What limitation of video-based world models does Code World Model target?
flashcards.back_html: Video models learn dynamics from visual observations, which reveal outcomes rather than the underlying knowledge, rules, and mechanisms — making persistent consequences and coherent open-ended evolution hard to maintain.

flashcards.prompt: In Code World Model, what connects the executable world state to the rendered video?

choices.text: A proxy representation encoding frame-wise spatiotemporal constraints, compiled into a proxy video that conditions the video model
A text description of each frame fed to the video model as a prompt
Direct fine-tuning of the video model on the coding agent's source code

flashcards.explanation_html: The proxy video is the interface: it carries the spatiotemporal constraints the code decided, and the video model renders high-fidelity observations conditioned on it.

flashcards.prompt: What role does the coding agent play in this framework?
flashcards.back_html: It's the 'world brain' — reasoning about events and their consequences, then generating executable code that maintains persistent world state and evolves it consistently with the rules.
